microtheory.name: intentionality_meaning
microtheory.definition: How mental states get their content. Aboutness. Reference, representation, semantic content. Brentano, Dretske, Fodor, Millikan. Substrate analogue: how substrate's Concepts come to be ABOUT things.

concepts.name: brentanos_thesis
concepts.definition: Brentano 1874. Intentionality is mark of the mental — every mental state directed at object. Substrate analogue: substrate's Concept→referent edges.

concepts.name: intentional_object
concepts.definition: What the mental state is about. May or may not exist. 'Belief that unicorns are white' — unicorn is intentional object. Substrate analogue: substrate's Concept referent.

concepts.name: directedness
concepts.definition: Mental states point at content. Substrate analogue: substrate's directed edges.

concepts.name: propositional_attitude
concepts.definition: Mental state with sentential complement. Believes that P, desires that P, fears that P. Substrate analogue: substrate's Concept-towards-proposition structure.

concepts.name: causal_theory_reference
concepts.definition: Kripke. Reference fixed by initial naming + causal chains. Names rigidly designate. Substrate analogue: substrate's instance-grounded Concept reference.

concepts.name: descriptive_theory_reference
concepts.definition: Frege, Russell. Reference fixed by description. 'The author of Waverley' refers to whoever satisfies. Substrate analogue: substrate's role-based Concept reference.

concepts.name: rigid_designator
concepts.definition: Kripke. Refers to same thing in every possible world. Proper names are rigid. Substrate analogue: substrate's persistent Concept identity.

concepts.name: twin_earth_externalism
concepts.definition: Putnam 1975. Doppelgangers on chemically-different Twin Earth referring to 'water' (XYZ vs H2O) have different meanings despite identical heads. Meaning ain't in the head. Substrate analogue: substrate's environment-dependent Concept content.

concepts.name: natural_meaning_grice
concepts.definition: 'Smoke means fire' — natural/indicative. Causal/nomological connection. Substrate analogue: substrate's causal-correlation Concept.

concepts.name: non_natural_meaning_grice
concepts.definition: Speaker means P by uttering X if intends hearer to recognize intent + thereby believe P. Substrate analogue: substrate's communicative-intent Message.

concepts.name: linguistic_meaning
concepts.definition: Conventional meaning of words + sentences. Truth conditions. Substrate analogue: substrate's lexicon-to-Concept mapping.

concepts.name: informational_semantics
concepts.definition: Dretske 1981. Mental state means P iff it carries information that P — under normal conditions. Substrate analogue: substrate's reliable-cause-Concept linking.

concepts.name: teleosemantics
concepts.definition: Millikan 1984. Mental content fixed by evolutionary function. State represents what it was selected to represent. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded-Concept teleological content.

concepts.name: asymmetric_dependence_theory
concepts.definition: Fodor 1990. X means cow iff cow→X and any non-cow→X depends on cow→X. Substrate analogue: substrate's prototype-grounded Concept.

concepts.name: conceptual_role_semantics
concepts.definition: Block, Harman. Meaning = role in inferential network. Substrate analogue: substrate's Concept-meaning = its edges.

concepts.name: narrow_content_v_wide_content
concepts.definition: Narrow = supervenes on intrinsic states; wide = includes environmental relations. Substrate analogue: substrate-only state vs substrate+environment state.

concepts.name: qualia_intentionalism
concepts.definition: Tye, Dretske. Phenomenal character = intentional content. Pain feels painful BECAUSE it represents bodily damage. Substrate analogue: substrate's qualia-as-representational-content view.

concepts.name: transparent_experience
concepts.definition: Looking out at world, we see world, not experience. Phenomenology is of objects, not of experience. Substrate analogue: substrate's transparent-introspection.

concepts.name: frame_problem_intentionality
concepts.definition: Fodor + Pylyshyn. How does cognitive system know which features of a situation are relevant? Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-relevance computation.

concepts.name: symbol_grounding_problem
concepts.definition: Harnad 1990. How do symbols get their meaning? Cannot be by other symbols (regress). Need world-coupling. Substrate analogue: substrate's grounding-by-action.

concepts.name: chinese_room_argument
concepts.definition: Searle 1980. Symbol manipulation without understanding. Argument against strong AI / computational mind. Substrate analogue: does substrate UNDERSTAND? Open.

concepts.name: mental_representation
concepts.definition: Internal state that represents something external. Map-like or sentence-like. Substrate analogue: substrate's Concept node + its edges.

concepts.name: concept
concepts.definition: Mental representation of category. Building block of thought. Prototype + exemplar + theory-based accounts. Substrate analogue: literally substrate's Concept node.

concepts.name: proposition
concepts.definition: Truth-evaluable content. Sharable between heads. Object of propositional attitudes. Substrate analogue: substrate's complex Concept structure.

rules.name: intentionality_marks_mental_states
rules.head: the substrate has a mental state
rules.body: that state is ABOUT something — has intentional content. Brentano. Substrate's Concept has directed edge to referent.

rules.name: causal_chain_grounds_reference
rules.head: the substrate refers to an entity with a name
rules.body: the reference is grounded in causal chain from initial naming. Kripke. Substrate's instance-grounded Concept.

rules.name: twin_earth_shows_externalism
rules.head: two substrates have identical internal states but differ in environment
rules.body: their mental contents differ. Meaning ain't in the head. Substrate's environment-dependent content.

rules.name: informational_semantics_links_content_to_reliability
rules.head: the substrate's state reliably tokens when X is present
rules.body: the state carries info about X + can be said to mean X under normal conditions. Dretske 1981.

rules.name: symbol_grounding_requires_world_coupling
rules.head: the substrate processes symbolic content
rules.body: the symbols must be grounded by world coupling, not just by other symbols. Harnad 1990. Substrate's grounding-by-action principle.
